A SHORT BOOK ON COGNITION

Chapter 1: Embodiment

The concept of embodiment is central to understanding cognition.
Cognitive scientists argue that the body is not merely a vessel for
the mind, but is constitutive of mental processes.

This view challenges the Cartesian split between mind and body.
It places perception, action, and conceptualization in a single
explanatory frame.

Chapter 2: Affordances

Affordances are action possibilities the environment offers an
agent. A chair affords sitting; a doorknob affords grasping.

These relations are real properties, not subjective projections.

Chapter 3: Conclusion

Embodied cognition reframes both philosophy of mind and AI design.
The implications are still unfolding.
